title: Finite evaluation normalization of compact-support exchanges and refinements
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring, $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type morphism of schemes, and $a:Y'\to Y$ any scheme morphism, with Cartesian pullback $f':X'\to Y'$ and $a_X:X'\to X$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Supply compactifications $c_i=(j_i:X\hookrightarrow\overline X_i,p_i:\overline X_i\to Y)$ with quasi-compact open $j_i$ and proper $p_i$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and their pullbacks $c_i'$ [pur713-def-base-changed-compactification]. Use strict constant-$\Lambda$ tower operations and evaluation $\operatorname{ev}_n$ with the normalized adjunction-mate direct-image comparison [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations, def-cbc-strict-tower-open-extension]. Put $F_i^{\mathcal T}=R_{p_i}^{\mathcal T}J_{j_i}$ and $F_i=Rp_{i,*}j_{i!}$ on ordinary constant-$\Lambda$ derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Let $e_i^{\mathcal T}:G_aF_i^{\mathcal T}\to(F_i')^{\mathcal T}G_{a_X}$ be the proper mate followed by the canonical open comparison; let $e_i$ be that same ordered compactification formula on ordinary complexes [def-exchange-projection]. For a proper refinement $u:c_1\to c_2$ fixing $X$, let $C_u^{\mathcal T}:F_2^{\mathcal T}\to F_1^{\mathcal T}$ be the normalized refinement map of [lem-cbc-complete-proetale-refinement-exchange-coherence], and let $C_u$ be the ordinary normalized proper/open refinement map, given on ordinary pro-etale complexes by the same proper-adjunction mate formula $\gamma$ as in [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] followed by the proper direct image; on bounded-below etale-origin objects it is the map of [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence].
For every $M\in D(\mathcal T_X)$ and every index $n$, the canonical evaluation comparisons identify $\operatorname{ev}_n(e_{i,M}^{\mathcal T})$ with $e_{i,\operatorname{ev}_nM}$ and $\operatorname{ev}_n(C_{u,M}^{\mathcal T})$ with $C_{u,\operatorname{ev}_nM}$. These identifications include the proper derived adjunction units and counits, not only underived maps. On the full domain where each $\operatorname{ev}_nM$ has a bounded-below etale-origin witness [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], the $C_u$ are isomorphisms and
$$C'_u e_2=e_1G_aC_u,\qquad C_{\mathrm{id}}=1,\qquad C_{v\circ u}=C_uC_v.$$
The induced $I_{12}=C_{u_2}^{-1}C_{u_1}$ from common refinements are independent of the refinement, satisfy $I_{23}I_{12}=I_{13}$, and intertwine $e_i$. Consequently compactification-relative pasting equations transport through these $I$ to the specified compactification-independent finite exchanges on the finite witnessed domain of [fix-lem-exchanges]. This conclusion applies in particular by taking a constant tower on any such finite complex. It asserts no faithfulness of derived evaluation.

proof.text: Put $N=\operatorname{ev}_nM$ and $B=\Lambda$. Apply [lem-cbc-tower-mate-evaluation-scalars] to obtain the canonical comparisons $\operatorname{ev}_nR_u^{\mathcal T}\cong Ru_*\operatorname{ev}_n$, together with the termwise comparisons for $G_u$ and $J_j$. The cited statement preserves the derived units, counits and transposes, for arbitrary unbounded tower objects. Its comparison is the K-injective resolution comparison and hence the adjunction-mate comparison specified in the item. Composition comparisons also agree: inverse-image compositors are termwise; their right-adjoint conjugates evaluate to the ordinary conjugates because the evaluation comparisons preserve the units and counits. Equivalently, [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization] identifies these conjugates with the resolution-normalized derived direct-image compositors. This fixes the comparisons for $R_{p_2}^{\mathcal T}R_u^{\mathcal T}$ as well as for a single direct image. Lean implementation: derived_adjunction_evaluation is the existing evaluation_units_counits theorem verbatim, and evaluationF_isIso follows by whiskering evalR_isIso and evalJ. presentation_isIso transports the adjunction across the finite-presentation equivalences using [lem-weil-mate-iso-along-equivalences]. The expanded composition exchange is identified with the relative compact-support tower exchange by the split-off compatibility statement.

source.place: Tags 07A7 (remark-base-change), 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition); strict-tower evaluation refinement supplied by the cited DAG statements.

proof.text: Write $\bar a_i:\overline X_i\times_Y Y'\to\overline X_i$. Expand the proper exchange using [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]: $E_{p_i}=(R_{p_i'}G_{\bar a_i}\varepsilon_{p_i})\circ(R_{p_i'}\theta_iR_{p_i})\circ(\eta_{p_i'}G_aR_{p_i})$, with the analogous tower formula. Step 1 carries each of its three factors to the displayed ordinary derived factor, since $\theta_i$ is the termwise pullback square comparison. By [lem-cbc-tower-open-beta-normalization], evaluation carries $\beta_{j_i,\bar a_i}^{\mathcal T}$ to the specified finite open comparison. Evaluation preserves composition and whiskering, so the evaluated ordered composite $(R_{p_i'}^{\mathcal T}\beta_{j_i,\bar a_i}^{\mathcal T})E_{p_i}^{\mathcal T}$ is precisely $(Rp_{i,*}'\beta_{j_i,\bar a_i})E_{p_i}$ at $N$, namely $e_{i,N}$. No boundedness or witness is used here.

source.place: Tag 07A7 (remark-base-change), unit-square-counit formula; open factor as in more-etale.tex Tag 0F7F (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-base-change).

proof.text: For a refinement $u:c_1\to c_2$, take the square $Q_u$ with top $j_1$, bottom $j_2$, left $1_X$ and right $u$. It has proper verticals and quasi-compact open horizontals. Its intrinsic $\alpha_{Q_u}$ is projection to the clopen section of $\overline X_1\times_{\overline X_2}X$ specified in [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. Apply [lem-cbc-tower-mate-evaluation-scalars]: evaluation of $\gamma_{Q_u}^{\mathcal T}=(R_u^{\mathcal T}J_{j_1}\varepsilon_1)\circ(R_u^{\mathcal T}\alpha_{Q_u}R_1^{\mathcal T})\circ(\eta_uJ_{j_2}R_1^{\mathcal T})$ is the ordinary proper mate of this same clopen projector. Now apply the $R_{p_2}$ comparison and the composition comparison fixed in step 1. Thus evaluation of $C_u^{\mathcal T}=R_{p_2}^{\mathcal T}\gamma_{Q_u}^{\mathcal T}$, with $R_{p_2}R_u\cong R_{p_1}$ inserted, is exactly $C_u$ at $N$. This argument applies to arbitrary $M$, not only witnessed objects.

source.place: Tags 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open), 0F7F (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-base-change); clopen mate and derived evaluation normalization are the cited refinements.

proof.text: On the witnessed domain, write $N\cong\nu_X^*L$ with $L\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$. By [lem-cbc-finite-clopen-mate-site-transport], the ordinary mate just obtained on $Q_u$ is the canonical transport of the normalized finite etale proper/open comparison; this is an isomorphism and includes the refinement normalization. Apply the ordinary $Rp_{2,*}$ to get the corresponding assertion for $C_u$. For exchanges apply [lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange] to the proper square for $p_i$, and combine it with the finite open comparison in [lem-cbc-tower-open-beta-normalization]. The direct-image transport hypotheses hold because $p_i,p_i'$ are proper, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and $j_{i!}L$ is bounded below by exactness of open extension. The resulting ordered composite is the transported etale compactification exchange, exactly the specified exchange of [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale]. Its hypotheses require a supplied compactification, which we have; they impose neither qcqs on the base nor a restriction on $a$ or on residue characteristics. Lean implementation: ordinaryGamma_etale is the identity-scalar specialization of [lem-cbc-single-level-finite-proper-open-transport]. Transport a retained fixed-module Origin to its etale antecedent using exact-derived composition, then use that equation and the proper direct-image comparison isomorphisms to show ordinaryC_isIso. pullOrigin applies the actual site pullback comparison and exact finite-presentation pullback comparison to the retained witness.

source.place: Tag 0F7F (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-base-change), finite etale proper/open square; pro-etale witness transport and mate normalization as in the cited DAG statements.

proof.text: Fix a witnessed finite complex $N$. Choose a representative complex and take its constant strict tower $\Delta N$, with identity transition maps. The constant-diagram construction is exact, since kernels and cokernels are levelwise, so this defines an object of $D(\mathcal T_X)$ independent of the representative. Every evaluation is $N$, and [lem-cbc-complete-proetale-refinement-exchange-coherence] applies with $B=\Lambda$, $\Lambda_r=\Lambda$ and the identity scalar maps at every index. Evaluate its actual tower identities $C'_ue_2=e_1G_aC_u$, $C_{\mathrm{id}}=1$, and $C_{v\circ u}=C_uC_v$ at any index. Steps 1-3 identify all the factors and compositors with the ordinary ones, so these are the required finite identities at $N$. For the original $M$ apply this argument separately to $N=\operatorname{ev}_nM$; no uniform lower bound is needed. Evaluation is used only to preserve already established equalities.

source.place: Tags 0F7C (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose), 0F7F (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-base-change); constant-tower specialization of the cited coherence statement.

proof.text: Common refinements and equalizers of parallel refinement arrows exist by [lem-cbc-compactifiable-cofiltered]. Passing from $d\xrightarrow{u_i}c_i$ to $d'\xrightarrow{t}d$ replaces $C_{u_i}$ by $C_tC_{u_i}$, hence leaves $C_{u_2}^{-1}C_{u_1}$ unchanged. Two choices admit a common refinement and then refinements equalizing their finitely many competing arrows; this proves independence of both objects and arrows. On one common refinement of three compactifications, $(C_3^{-1}C_2)(C_2^{-1}C_1)=C_3^{-1}C_1$, proving the cocycle. Writing $C_i'e_i=e_dG_aC_i$ twice and cancelling gives $I_{12}'e_1=e_2G_aI_{12}$. Finally, a compactification-relative pasting equation is an equality of composites. Replacing its corners by these isomorphisms replaces each arrow $h:A\to B$ by $I_BhI_A^{-1}$; intermediate inverse pairs cancel and the cocycle identifies the exterior comparisons. Thus the pasting equation holds for the compactification-independent exchanges. Step 4 identifies these with the specified finite maps on the domain of [fix-lem-exchanges]; this uses that domain and its specified maps, not its coherence theorem as a premise. Taking $M=\Delta N$ gives the last assertion. Lean implementation: equalize parallel refinements by cofilteredness and cancel ordinaryC of the equalizing arrow; composition then shows the ratio is unchanged by a further refinement. A common cone proves independence; a common cone for two of three pairs gives the cocycle by cancelling the middle inverse. ordinaryI_exchange follows from two instances of ordinaryC_exchange by cancelling the second primed refinement. transport_pasting is associativity, inverse cancellation, and the supplied pasting equality.
